summary: Every subplan except Computational Biology takes the School of Engineering math (26 units, including two math electives), science (11 units) and engineering fundamentals (10 units); Computational Biology has its own math, biology and fundamentals rules. Each depth needs 25 units across its track rules, and electives come from the lists the subplan names, with at most one humanities course where the subplan allows it. Every course must be letter graded with a D- or better, and a course counts toward one requirement only; the one exception is that your WIM course may also be your capstone (CS 191W, 194W, 210B) or Technology in Society course (CS 121, 182W), so check by hand that it does not also fill an elective. The major needs 93 units, or 86 in Computational Biology. You also check by hand the Technology in Society and science elective courses from the School of Engineering lists, the Computational Biology fundamentals elective, the 2.0 GPA over fundamentals, core, depth and senior project, an Individually Designed track's approval and courses, and for honors the 3.6 GPA, seminar and thesis. Left: the Computer Engineering "Required Elective Options" (CS 240, 240LX, 241, 244C, EE 179) has no text and stays required for every Computer Engineering student, though it may belong only to the Networking concentration.
